## Purpose

Rank candidate mutation contrasts on genotype and design grounds, before any
metabolomics result for them is looked at. For each candidate gene, report how
many mutant and wild-type lines inform a model with tissue as blocking factor,
which tissues contribute, whether the groups are balanced across culture
batches, whether the design is estimable, which other alterations go with the
mutation, and whether it can serve as a positive control.

**Decision supported:** choice of contrast(s) and design formula (Checkpoint 2),
the definition of "mutated" per gene (Q1) and the minimum group sizes (Q2).

## Inputs

- `data/derived/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_v1/shorthouse_analysis_v1.rds` (lines used in models, DepMap status, ion annotation)
- `data/raw/cancer-cell-lines/msb202211006-sup-0005-datasetev4.xlsx` (genes tested by Shorthouse et al.)
- `config.yml`: `landscape` and `contrast` parameters

## Methods

Candidate genes were those altered in at least `min_altered_lines` lines in
the mutation landscape (analysis/02) plus genes named in the planning (EGFR,
KEAP1, NFE2L2, IDH1, IDH2, MTAP). Each was evaluated under two definitions of
"mutated": a likely-driver variant or homozygous deletion, and any
protein-changing variant or homozygous deletion. With tissue as blocking
factor, only tissues containing at least `min_per_group_per_tissue` mutant and
wild-type lines inform the mutation effect; their lines give the effective
group sizes. Balance across culture batches was tested on the contributing
lines with Fisher's exact test (simulated p-value). Estimability of the design
`~ batch + tissue + mutation` on the contributing lines was checked by the rank
of the design matrix, and its residual degrees of freedom reported. Co-occurring
alterations were summarised as the difference in the share of altered lines
between mutant and wild-type lines. No metabolomics data are used in this
notebook.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/use_case.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/plotting.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/mutations.R"))
config <- load_config()
derived_dir <- uc_dir(config, "derived")
raw_dir <- uc_dir(config, "raw")
output_dir <- uc_dir(config, "output", "03_contrast_selection")
params <- config$contrast
set.seed(params$seed)

data <- readRDS(file.path(derived_dir, "shorthouse_analysis_v1.rds"))
lines <- filter(data$lines, in_models)

# genes tested by Shorthouse et al. plus MTAP (as in analysis/02)
ev4 <- readxl::read_excel(file.path(raw_dir, "msb202211006-sup-0005-datasetev4.xlsx"), sheet = "Sheet1", n_max = 1)
genes <- union(sub("^T_", "", setdiff(names(ev4), "ionIdx")), "MTAP")
status <- alteration_status(data, lines$line, genes) %>%
    mutate(
        mutated_driver = likely_driver | deleted,   # definition A
        mutated_any = any_mutation | deleted        # definition B
    )

# candidates: genes reaching the landscape threshold under definition A, plus planning genes
landscape_genes <- status %>%
    group_by(gene) %>%
    summarise(n = sum(mutated_driver), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(n >= config$landscape$min_altered_lines) %>%
    pull(gene)
candidates <- union(landscape_genes, params$extra_genes)
c(lines = nrow(lines), candidates = length(candidates))
```

## 1. Effective group sizes with tissue as blocking factor

```{r effective-n}
# per candidate, definition and tissue: mutant and wild-type lines
per_tissue <- status %>%
    filter(gene %in% candidates) %>%
    pivot_longer(c(mutated_driver, mutated_any), names_to = "definition", values_to = "mutated") %>%
    mutate(definition = recode(definition, mutated_driver = "A: likely driver or deletion",
                               mutated_any = "B: any protein-changing or deletion")) %>%
    group_by(gene, definition, tissue) %>%
    summarise(mutant = sum(mutated), wild_type = sum(!mutated), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(contributes = mutant >= params$min_per_group_per_tissue &
               wild_type >= params$min_per_group_per_tissue)

effective <- per_tissue %>%
    group_by(gene, definition) %>%
    summarise(
        mutant_all = sum(mutant),
        effective_mutant = sum(mutant[contributes]),
        effective_wild_type = sum(wild_type[contributes]),
        n_tissues = sum(contributes),
        tissues = paste(sprintf("%s (%d/%d)", tissue[contributes], mutant[contributes], wild_type[contributes]),
                        collapse = ", "),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(definition, desc(effective_mutant))
preview_table(effective, caption = "Effective group sizes (tissue: mutant/wild-type)")

p <- effective %>%
    filter(effective_mutant > 0) %>%
    ggplot(aes(effective_mutant, reorder(gene, effective_mutant, max), fill = definition)) +
    geom_col(position = "dodge") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = params$min_mutant_total, linetype = 2) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#D55E00", "#0072B2")) +
    labs(x = "Mutant lines in contributing tissues", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
         title = "Effective number of mutant lines with tissue as blocking factor",
         subtitle = sprintf("contributing tissue: >= %d mutant and >= %d wild-type lines; dashed: minimum %d",
                            params$min_per_group_per_tissue, params$min_per_group_per_tissue, params$min_mutant_total)) +
    theme_uc() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
save_figure(p, "effective_n", output_dir, width = 8, height = 8)
p
```

## 2. Design checks for the candidates

```{r design}
ranked <- filter(effective, effective_mutant >= params$min_mutant_total)

# for each remaining candidate: batch balance and estimability on the contributing lines
check_design <- function(g, def) {
    col <- if (startsWith(def, "A")) "mutated_driver" else "mutated_any"
    contributing <- per_tissue %>% filter(gene == g, definition == def, contributes) %>% pull(tissue)
    d <- status %>% filter(gene == g, tissue %in% contributing) %>%
        transmute(line, tissue, batch, mutated = .data[[col]])
    batch_p <- if (n_distinct(d$batch) > 1) {
        fisher.test(table(d$batch, d$mutated), simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 1e4)$p.value
    } else NA_real_
    # tissue and batch enter the design only if they have more than one level
    terms <- c(if (n_distinct(d$batch) > 1) "batch", if (n_distinct(d$tissue) > 1) "tissue", "mutated")
    X <- model.matrix(reformulate(terms), data = d)
    rank <- qr(X)$rank
    tibble(gene = g, definition = def, lines = nrow(d), batches = n_distinct(d$batch),
           batch_balance_p = batch_p, full_rank = rank == ncol(X), residual_df = nrow(d) - rank)
}
design_checks <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(ranked)), function(i) check_design(ranked$gene[i], ranked$definition[i])))
candidate_table <- ranked %>% left_join(design_checks, by = c("gene", "definition"))
preview_table(candidate_table, caption = "Candidates meeting the minimum, with design checks")
```

## 3. Co-occurring alterations

For the candidates, the share of lines carrying another alteration among
mutant and wild-type lines of the contributing tissues (definition A). Large
differences mark co-mutations that a model should include as covariates, or
that make a "mutant vs rest" contrast compare against another driver.

```{r comutations, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 7}
co_genes <- union(landscape_genes, params$extra_genes)
comutation <- bind_rows(lapply(unique(filter(candidate_table, startsWith(definition, "A"))$gene), function(g) {
    contributing <- per_tissue %>% filter(gene == g, startsWith(definition, "A"), contributes) %>% pull(tissue)
    groups <- status %>% filter(gene == g, tissue %in% contributing) %>% select(line, mutant = mutated_driver)
    status %>%
        filter(gene %in% setdiff(co_genes, g), line %in% groups$line) %>%
        inner_join(groups, by = "line") %>%
        group_by(co_gene = gene) %>%
        summarise(share_in_mutant = mean(mutated_driver[mutant]),
                  share_in_wild_type = mean(mutated_driver[!mutant]), .groups = "drop") %>%
        mutate(gene = g, difference = share_in_mutant - share_in_wild_type)
}))
comutation %>% arrange(desc(abs(difference))) %>% preview_table(caption = "Co-occurring alterations (definition A)")

p <- ggplot(comutation, aes(co_gene, gene, fill = difference)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#0072B2", mid = "white", high = "#D55E00", midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1)) +
    labs(x = "Other alteration", y = "Candidate", fill = "Share in mutant\nminus wild type",
         title = "Co-occurring (red) and exclusive (blue) alterations within the contributing tissues") +
    theme_uc() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
save_figure(p, "comutations", output_dir, width = 11, height = 7)
p
```

## 4. Positive controls

Genotypes with an expected metabolic readout (planning): KEAP1/NFE2L2 →
glutathione; MTAP deletion → 5'-methylthioadenosine; IDH1/2 →
2-hydroxyglutarate. Readout ions are looked up by name in the annotation
(see audit/05); only availability is reported, not their values.

```{r positive-controls}
readout_patterns <- c(KEAP1 = "glutathione", NFE2L2 = "glutathione", MTAP = "methylthioadenosine",
                      IDH1 = "hydroxyglutar", IDH2 = "hydroxyglutar")
readouts <- tibble(gene = names(readout_patterns), pattern = readout_patterns) %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(
        readout_ions = sum(grepl(pattern, tolower(data$ions$name))),
        unambiguous_readout_ions = sum(grepl(pattern, tolower(data$ions$name)) & !grepl(";", data$ions$name))
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
effective %>%
    filter(gene %in% names(readout_patterns)) %>%
    select(gene, definition, mutant_all, effective_mutant, effective_wild_type, tissues) %>%
    left_join(readouts, by = "gene") %>%
    preview_table(caption = "Positive-control genotypes: group sizes and readout ions")
```

## Interpretation and recommendation

- **Definition of "mutated" (Q1):** definition B (any protein-changing variant)
  inflates long genes with many passenger variants (MUC4, MUC16, LRP1B, CSMD3)
  but captures loss-of-function genes better: KEAP1 has 8 mutant lung lines
  under A and 19 under B. A per-gene choice is therefore needed: likely-driver
  variants for oncogenes (KRAS, NRAS, BRAF, PIK3CA, EGFR, NFE2L2), any
  protein-changing variant or homozygous deletion for tumour suppressors (TP53,
  STK11, KEAP1, SMARCA4, CDKN2A, PTEN, RB1); long passenger-prone genes are not
  candidates.
- **TP53** is altered in most lines (110 mutant vs 36 wild-type lines in
  contributing tissues); it is better used as a covariate than as a contrast.
- **KRAS** (30 mutant / 67 wild-type lines in lung, colon and blood; mostly
  lung, 25/61) is balanced across batches and estimable with
  `~ batch + tissue + mutation`. KRAS-mutant lines carry fewer TP53
  alterations, so TP53 belongs in the model; STK11 and KEAP1 are planned
  covariates for lung.
- **Lung-only contrasts:** STK11 (19/67 under A, 22/64 under B), SMARCA4
  (15/71) and KEAP1 (8/78 under A, 19/67 under B) are informed by lung lines
  only. KEAP1 together with NFE2L2 (5 mutant lung lines) defines NRF2
  activation, whose readout (glutathione ions) is measured unambiguously; this
  is the best available positive control. Combining them is a pathway-level
  aggregation and needs your approval (Q3).
- **MTAP deletion** (32/114 in six tissues) is well powered and balanced, and
  metabolically direct (methionine salvage), but its readout MTA is not
  measured, and it is nested in CDKN2A deletion (94 % of MTAP-deleted lines),
  so the two cannot be separated.
- **Batch imbalance** (p < 0.05) affects RB1, ARID1A and FAT1; these need care.

**Recommendation:**

1. Positive control first: **NRF2 activation (KEAP1 or NFE2L2 altered) in
   lung**, design `~ batch + KRAS + STK11 + TP53 + NRF2`, expected readout
   glutathione-related ions.
2. Main contrast: **KRAS mutant vs wild type with tissue as blocking factor**,
   design `~ batch + tissue + TP53 + STK11 + KEAP1 + KRAS` (co-mutation
   covariates only where they vary within the contributing tissues).
3. Optional second contrast: **MTAP deletion** across tissues,
   `~ batch + tissue + TP53 + MTAP`, interpreted as 9p21 (MTAP/CDKN2A) loss.

```{r save}
readr::write_csv(effective, file.path(output_dir, "effective_group_sizes.csv"))
readr::write_csv(candidate_table, file.path(output_dir, "candidates.csv"))
readr::write_csv(comutation, file.path(output_dir, "comutations.csv"))
```
